Masked Erosion has already done that for deletions, and SHarP and RB-Prompt already handle the length reduction. The per-surface DFE is interesting and new. The paper would be stronger if the DFE and the two-sided bloat/erosion prediction were the contribution and the analogy were left out.

title: Synthetic Drift Lies About Harness Learners: Rank Disagreement and Overstated Forgetting Relative to Matched Real Histories
claim: For 6 continual harness-learning methods, ranks on synthetic drift streams agree poorly with ranks on real-history streams matched to them in change count and era length (Kendall τ < 0.4). Synthetic streams also overstate forgetting by at least 1.5×, and the overstatement grows with how abrupt the synthetic transitions are.
alt: If ranks agree (τ > 0.7) and forgetting is matched, synthetic streams are validated as cheap proxies, a useful methodological result that licenses Δτ/AgentDriftBench-style benchmarks and saves the field from costly real mining. In either case the paired real/synthetic suite is released.
law: Forgetting_synth / Forgetting_real ≈ 1 + γ · A, where A ∈ [0,1] is the abruptness of the synthetic transitions. The prediction is γ > 0, with γ near zero when the real stream is itself abrupt (removal releases). This is the harness-learner analogue of hip2PfZSRg.
pilot:
Use the API source only (2 libraries, 3 eras), 3 methods (ICL, GEPA-style, Gödel-lite), the synthetic twin at abrupt and gradual settings, and 3 seeds on Qwen3-14B. About $25 for drafting the twins.
Go if at least one pairwise rank flip between real and abrupt-synthetic appears across seeds with non-overlapping CIs, or if forgetting differs by at least 1.3×.
Kill if every metric matches within CI. In that case reframe as a validation note and fold the infrastructure into the first idea.
closest: Δτ-Bench 2610.34238 and AgentDriftBench 5xFWggnePr use synthetic drift only. Are-SE-CL 2610.25858 uses synthetic block streams. hip2PfZSRg ('Do NNs Lose Plasticity in a Gradually Changing World?') addresses weight-level plasticity, not harness learners. WebVariants TYSv9rIhiQ shows rank reversals across implementations, not across real versus synthetic drift. None measures agreement between real and synthetic drift for harness learners.

judges.strongest: The gap is real and checkable. No 2026 paper or ICLR 2027 submission tests whether the synthetic drift generators (Delta-tau-Bench, AgentDriftBench, ProEvolve) give the same conclusions about continual harness learners as real release histories do. The forgetting-ratio vs abruptness law (gamma > 0, with gamma about 0 on real abrupt removal releases as a built-in falsification check) is a sharp, falsifiable, quantitative claim. It speaks to the user's question about a benchmark grounded in reality, and the paired real/synthetic suite is a reusable artifact whichever way the result goes.
judges.weakest: The abruptness axis is confounded, and the direction of the prediction may be wrong. Real API, schema and web releases are step changes at release tags, so the 'all changes at the era boundary' twin is arguably the most realistic one, and a 'gradual' twin has no real counterpart. If so, gamma measures how far the twin departs from the real step shape, not how much synthetic streams overstate forgetting. The same problem hits the forgetting metric. Dormant-return probes need old versions to come back, and real histories rarely revert, so the real-side forgetting signal either barely exists or has to be built synthetically. That would make the comparison circular. On top of this, Kendall tau over 6 methods is badly underpowered. The cost is also large: 6 methods x 2 models x 5 seeds x 3 sources x 4 conditions (real plus 3 abruptness levels), on top of three separate real-mining pipelines, which a solo undergrad with $3k will struggle to deliver. The idea also depends on the DriftEras/ContractPatch/BreakingWeb infrastructure from other ideas. It is a methods-validation side study, only loosely tied to the user's main questions (how open the search space is vs how effective the system is, why meta-harnesses rarely update themselves).
judges.mustFix: (1) Define abruptness for the real streams themselves: measure each real stream's empirical A, using deprecation windows, staged rollouts and multi-release migrations. Then regress the forgetting ratio on the gap A_synth - A_real, not on A_synth alone. Include a twin that matches A_real as the null condition. (2) Define forgetting on the real side without synthetic reverts. Options are long-tail tasks that go dormant and then reappear in later real eras, or backward-compatibility probes on still-supported old endpoints. (3) Replace the 6-method Kendall tau with pairwise-preference agreement (15+ pairs x streams x seeds) under a hierarchical bootstrap, and add 2-3 cheap methods. (4) Match twins on edit-type mix (rename/split/remove/semantic) as well as change count. Add an ablation that matches edit type but changes only the generator, to separate 'synthetic' from 'edit-type' effects. (5) Cut scope: one model at full depth (Qwen3-14B), with 32B for a single replication; at most 2 real sources (API plus MCP/OpenAPI); TimeWarp as the web fallback. (6) Run it as the validation chapter of the DriftEras paper rather than as a standalone submission. A 'synthetic is a fine proxy' null result on its own reads as a workshop note.
judges.reviewerQuote: "The authors claim synthetic drift overstates forgetting as transitions become more abrupt. But the real streams they compare against are release-tag step functions, which are maximally abrupt. Without measuring the real streams' own abruptness, and without a forgetting signal on the real side that does not depend on synthetic reverts, I cannot tell whether gamma measures how synthetic the stream is or just a mismatch in schedule shape. Rank agreement over six methods with five seeds also lacks the power to support the tau < 0.4 headline. title: Permissions Don't Matter, Realized Edits Do: Effective Openness Mediates the Effect of the Editable Surface on Held-Out Self-Improvement
claim: Across rungs and optimizers, held-out gain is predicted by effective openness H_eff (entropy over executable reachability classes of accepted edits). Nominal permission level adds no predictive power once H_eff is controlled for. Raising H_eff at a fixed nominal rung raises gain along the same curve, and widening permissions without raising H_eff does not.
alt: If nominal rung keeps significant explanatory power beyond H_eff, then which mechanisms are reachable matters even when they are rarely used: for example, the option to edit the improver changes proposer behavior elsewhere. That supports design-space-first work in the RegNet/NAS style and is publishable as 'the space, not the walk'. If H_eff interventions raise H_eff but lower gain, diversity per se is harmful at this budget. That is a clean negative against diversity-forcing methods (EvoSpace, DyScope-style widening).
design: This reuses the LadderLoop runs from openness-ladder-crossover and adds causal arms. H_eff is computed from each accepted edit, which is classified automatically into reachability classes: AST diff with a file/function target; a semantic class (hyperparameter/knob, prompt text, control-flow mechanism, new tool or state, improver logic, selection logic) assigned by a frozen classifier and validated on 200 hand-labelled edits with Cohen's κ; and structural-revisit rate (as in 2606.05408). H_eff is the Shannon entropy of the class mass over accepted edits, alongside a 'novel-mechanism mass'. The 27B optimizer runs at rungs L2, L3 and L4, with 5 seeds and 2M matched tokens each, in four arms. A0 is the baseline. A1 raises H_eff at fixed rung: target-file rotation plus a class-coverage bonus in the proposal prompt, with the gate unchanged. A2 widens nominal permission one rung while freezing H_eff, using rejection sampling of proposals so the class distribution matches the lower rung. A3 lowers H_eff, restricting proposals to the modal class. Tasks are CO-Bench (exact) and tau2/AppWorld (noisy), with a sealed held-out split. The analysis is a mediation analysis (rung → H_eff → gain) with lineage-level bootstrap, plus a curve-collapse test: fit gain = f(H_eff) on the A0 arms and predict the A1, A2 and A3 cells out of sample, comparing that against a rung-based model by held-out-cell RMSE.
law: Gain_heldout ≈ g(H_eff) with g concave (rising then saturating or declining). The pre-registered prediction is a single collapse curve across rungs and arms, and the rung coefficient is ≈0 conditional on H_eff (equivalence bound ±0.25 seed-SD).
pilot: Week 1, about $35 with local 27B. Re-code the pilot lineages from openness-ladder-crossover (L1/L3/L4) plus 2 seeds of A1 at L3. Go if (i) classifier κ ≥ 0.7 on 100 hand-labelled edits, (ii) A1 raises H_eff by ≥0.5 bits over A0 without halving the acceptance rate, and (iii) H_eff varies by ≥1 bit across the A0 lineages. Kill if H_eff cannot be moved by cheap interventions: realized openness would then be fixed by the proposer prior, and the result folds into idea 3's behavioral analysis.
closest: Mutation Without Variation 2606.05408 (revisit entropy, but no selection and no link to gain). Reachability study oTYVUBHmbe (76% knob edits, but a single surface and no mediation test). HarnessOpt-Bench 2608.06301 (lever coverage correlates with gain, but this is observational and confounded with the optimizer). Opinionated Optimizers LhhLpXBFgo (narrow proposer priors, descriptive only). EvoSpace MQoRwlss2y and DyScope MXINrso5QC (adapt scope as a method, with no causal or collapse test). Delta: the first interventional test of whether realized, rather than permitted, openness is the causal variable, plus a collapse-curve law.

check.reposition:
RobustSGPO (2609.09646) already introduces S_nom vs S_real vs S_eff. It already claims that broader permissions do not by themselves help, and it shows that category-directed control at fixed permission raises realized coverage and held-out quality. So 'first to distinguish permitted from realized openness' and 'first interventional evidence' will not survive. The claim also has to absorb the null results of oTYVUBHmbe and 2610.30499.

1. Cite RobustSGPO as the source of the nominal/realized distinction and of the single-workflow intervention. Present the contribution as the formal causal test it lacks: mediation with a pre-registered equivalence bound on the rung coefficient, and the A2 arm (widen permission while freezing the realized class distribution by rejection sampling). No neighbour runs A2, so make it the headline experiment.
2. Make the generality claim carry the paper: more than one optimizer (the 27B model plus one frontier optimizer and a GEPA/OpenEvolve-style baseline), an exact task (CO-Bench) and noisy tasks (tau2/AppWorld), and out-of-sample curve-collapse prediction across optimizers. RobustSGPO is one industrial workflow with an LLM-judged 0-5 score.
3. Use effective (accepted and valid) entropy, not coverage, and show it beats RobustSGPO-style coverage and HarnessOpt-Bench lever coverage as a predictor of held-out-cell RMSE. Otherwise H_eff is just a renamed coverage metric.
4. Make novel-mechanism mass co-primary and pre-register the competing hypothesis from oTYVUBHmbe: realized novelty raises the search-set score but not held-out gain, which is the elicitation story of 2610.27889. Frame the result as a two-sided test, 'which openness variable carries the effect, if any', so that a null curve is still publishable.
5. Separate A1 from RobustSGPO's planned category sampling and DyScope's target redirection. Either adopt their controller as A1, which credits them and makes this a replication across optimizers, or show that class-coverage bonus prompting is a distinct manipulation. Report the cost per unit of H_eff raised.

judges.strongest: The A2 arm is the one experiment no neighbour has run: widen nominal permission while holding the realized edit-class distribution fixed. It is a clean interventional handle on "permissions vs. realized edits". The two-sided framing (H_eff carries the effect / rung carries it / diversity hurts) makes every outcome publishable. It also reuses the LadderLoop runs, so the marginal cost is low.
judges.weakest: The mediator is mechanically tied to the outcome. H_eff is computed over ACCEPTED edits, and acceptance is gated on search-set improvement. So lineages with more or more varied accepted edits will show both higher entropy and higher gain by construction. This is selection-induced (collider-like) correlation, not mediation. The entropy estimate is also biased by the number of accepted edits. Separately, the equivalence claim is badly underpowered. Roughly 12 cells per task (3 rungs x 4 arms) with 5 seeds cannot support a TOST at ±0.25 seed-SD: you need on the order of 100+ seeds per contrast. A2's rejection sampling freezes H_eff by construction, so 'rung adds nothing under A2' only tests within-class content, and the rejection sampling itself shifts the proposer distribution. On top of that, RobustSGPO has already taken the nominal/realized framing and the A1-style intervention, so novelty rests almost entirely on A2 plus a curve fit.
judges.mustFix: (1) Define the mediator on PROPOSED or pre-gate edits, or on a fixed-size subsample of accepted edits, with a count-matched entropy estimator such as Miller-Madow or rarefaction. Report that it still predicts gain after controlling for the number of accepted edits. Otherwise the H_eff-gain link is a selection artifact. (2) Replace the ±0.25 seed-SD equivalence bound with a power-justified one. Either commit roughly 20+ seeds on the key L3-vs-L4 A0/A2 contrast, or pre-register a wide bound and call the result 'no large rung effect'. (3) Make A2 the headline experiment, and add an A2-placebo: rejection sampling at the SAME rung, to separate the effect of the sampling procedure from the permission change. (4) Credit RobustSGPO for the distinction and for the A1-style control, and pre-register the oTYVUBHmbe / 2610.30499 null as a competing hypothesis. Show that H_eff beats coverage fraction on held-out-cell RMSE. (5) Fold this in as the causal section of openness-ladder-crossover rather than a standalone paper, and keep any frontier optimizer to a small cross-check within budget.
judges.reviewerQuote: "The authors compute their 'causal mediator' over edits that were accepted precisely because they improved the score, then report that it predicts the score. Without a pre-gate or count-matched definition, and with five seeds supporting an equivalence claim at a quarter of a seed-SD, the mediation analysis cannot carry the headline. The widen-but-freeze arm is genuinely interesting and deserves to be the paper, but RobustSGPO already owns the permitted-versus-realized framing."

judges.strongest: The A2 arm is the one design element no neighbor has: it widens the permission while holding the realized class distribution fixed. Combined with an out-of-sample curve-collapse test against a rung-only model, it makes the question 'is permitted or realized openness the causal variable' sharp and falsifiable. It also sits right in the mentor's area (how much freedom a self-referential improver should have) and directly addresses the user's question of whether there is a law relating openness to effectiveness.
judges.weakest: The causal logic is close to circular. (1) H_eff is computed over ACCEPTED edits, and the gate accepts edits based on search-set gain. So H_eff is a post-treatment variable that partly depends on the outcome: lineages that find gains get more accepted edits of more kinds, which inflates entropy. Mediation rung -> H_eff -> gain then fails sequential ignorability, and the reverse path gain -> H_eff can produce the 'collapse' with no causal effect of openness at all. (2) A2 freezes the class distribution by rejection sampling, which cuts away exactly the edits the wider rung newly allows. Wider permission then mostly exists only on paper, so 'rung adds nothing given H_eff' is nearly true by construction. Reviewers will call the headline null on rung tautological. (3) RobustSGPO (2609.09646) already holds the nominal/realized framing and the A1-style intervention, and oTYVUBHmbe and 2610.30499 supply counter-data. What remains is a stats-and-generality upgrade, not a new phenomenon. On top of that, the 'law' is a concave fit on 3 rungs x 4 arms, about 12 cells, which is thin for a collapse claim.
judges.mustFix: Measure openness on PROPOSED edits (pre-gate), or on a fixed, gain-independent sample of them, and report accepted-edit H_eff only as a secondary measure. That removes the outcome-dependence of the mediator. Redesign A2 so that the widened permission is actually exercised at a controlled rate: for example, force k% of proposals into the newly unlocked class while matching total entropy by reweighting the other classes. Then 'permission without entropy change' becomes a real manipulation instead of a filter. Add a dose-response design with at least 3 graded levels of the A1 bonus per rung (≥9-12 interventional cells) so that g(H_eff) is identified from intervention rather than observation. Make the predictor contest the pre-registered primary test: H_eff vs coverage fraction (RobustSGPO) vs lever coverage (HarnessOpt-Bench) vs novel-mechanism mass, scored by held-out-cell RMSE. Drop the 'first interventional' claim. Cap the token budget realistically: 3 rungs x 4 arms x 5 seeds x 2 task families x 2M tokens comes to about 240M optimizer tokens plus evaluation, before adding the frontier optimizer the reposition requires. Either cut the noisy-task family to 3 seeds or run the frontier optimizer at L3 only. Given that it reuses the openness-ladder-crossover runs, this works best as the mechanism section of that paper rather than as a standalone paper.
judges.reviewerQuote: The authors condition on entropy over accepted edits, but acceptance is decided by the very gain they are trying to predict. The A2 arm freezes the class distribution by rejecting everything the wider permission newly enables. I am not convinced the finding that nominal permission does not matter is anything more than a consequence of the design, and the nominal-vs-realized distinction itself was already made by RobustSGPO.

judges.strongest: The A2 arm is the one new piece: widen nominal permission, then use rejection sampling to hold the realized edit-class distribution at the lower rung's level. It directly tests whether having an option you don't use changes proposer behavior. No neighbour runs it, it fits Yin's Gödel-Agent line of work on whether the improver can improve itself, and it is cheap because it reuses the LadderLoop runs.
judges.weakest: Two problems: the framing is largely scooped, and the causal identification is weak. RobustSGPO (2609.09646) already separates nominal, realized and effective openness, and already shows that category-directed proposals at fixed permission raise coverage and held-out quality. The mediation design is also shaky. H_eff is a post-treatment variable that shares a cause with gain (proposer competence and acceptance by the gate). A1 is a prompt change, so it changes edit quality as well as entropy, which breaks the exclusion assumption. A2's rejection sampling at most adds a reweighting term on top of the lower rung. And the concave g(H_eff), with a rising-then-falling option, can fit almost any outcome, so the 'law' is barely falsifiable. oTYVUBHmbe and 2610.30499 already give null or counter-data on exact tasks. Compute is also tight. 3 rungs x 4 arms x 5 seeds x 2+ tasks is about 120 runs at 2M tokens each, roughly 240M tokens on a local 27B model. That is weeks of GPU time on modest hardware, before adding the frontier optimizer the repositioning needs.
judges.mustFix: (1) Make A2 the headline and add a placebo arm in which the higher-rung permission is granted but the proposer is never told about it. This separates 'knowing the option exists' from 'the option exists'. (2) Replace the mediation story with a pre-registered equivalence test on the rung coefficient across the interventional arms only, plus an out-of-sample collapse prediction on held-out cells. Commit to a specific functional form for g, for example a saturating curve fitted on A0 with its parameters frozen, so the law can actually fail. (3) Make A1 entropy-only: keep the prompt text identical and change only the target-file schedule, so the arm doesn't also change edit quality. Report the cost per bit of H_eff. (4) Show that H_eff beats RobustSGPO coverage and HarnessOpt-Bench lever coverage on held-out RMSE, or drop the entropy branding. (5) Cut the grid to 2 rungs x 4 arms x 5 seeds on CO-Bench plus one noisy task, and add a second open optimizer rather than a frontier one to stay within $3k. Realistically, this belongs as the mechanism/causal section of the openness-ladder-crossover paper, not as a standalone submission.
